description: This source file defines a generator for creating apply configuration types in Kubernetes code generation. It includes methods for generating struct definitions, getters, 'with' functions, constructors, and extraction functions for Kubernetes resource types, facilitating declarative configuration and apply workflows.

classes.name: applyConfigurationGenerator
classes.description: A generator class responsible for producing apply configuration code for Kubernetes resource types, including struct definitions, getters, setters, constructors, and extraction functions.

methods.name: GenerateType
methods.description: Generates the apply configuration struct, constructors, getters, and 'with' functions for a given resource type.

methods.name: generateGetters
methods.description: Creates getter methods for resource members in the apply configuration struct.

methods.name: generateWithFuncs
methods.description: Creates 'With' methods to set resource members in the apply configuration, supporting chaining.

methods.name: generateStruct
methods.description: Generates the struct definition for the apply configuration type.

methods.name: generateIsApplyConfiguration
methods.description: Creates a marker method to identify apply configuration types.

methods.name: generateMemberWith
methods.description: Creates a 'With' method for a specific member.

methods.name: generateMemberGetter
methods.description: Creates a getter method for a specific member.

methods.name: generateMemberWithForSlice
methods.description: Creates a 'With' method for slice members.

methods.name: generateMemberWithForMap
methods.description: Creates a 'With' method for map members.

methods.name: ensureEmbedExistsIfApplicable
methods.description: Ensures embedded types are initialized if needed.

methods.name: generateClientgenExtract
methods.description: Generates functions to extract apply configurations from resource objects.

methods.name: collectSubresources
methods.description: Collects subresource names like 'status' or custom extensions for extraction functions.
